input: Write a short biography for my memoir class

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A biography can cover a whole life, a defining era, or a single pivotal moment — the scope entirely shapes what gets written.
It is unclear whether this is a biography about themselves, someone else, or a composite — this changes the voice and sourcing entirely.
Word count or page length is likely prescribed by the class; writing 200 words versus 1,000 words requires a completely different level of depth.
Knowing the class assignment prompt or instructor guidelines would reveal what the biography is meant to demonstrate or practice.
Memoir writing ranges from confessional and vulnerable to reserved and literary — the tone and style the user wants will define the voice.
The user may want to impress an instructor, meet a rubric, explore personal growth, or simply get a draft done — this changes how polished and purposeful the output needs to be.
Knowing the deadline and what the user already has (notes, an outline, prior drafts) determines where to start and how much scaffolding is needed.

gold.taskTitle: Write a short biography for memoir class
gold.taskDescription: The user needs to write a short biography, likely about themselves, for a memoir writing class.

questions.title: Who is the biography actually about?
questions.description: Is this a biography about yourself, another person such as a family member, or a character inspired by someone real?

questions.title: What life period or theme should it focus on?
questions.description: Should the biography cover your entire life, a specific era (childhood, a career), or one defining moment or theme?

questions.title: What is the required word count or page length?
questions.description: Has your instructor specified a length — for example, 250 words, 500 words, or one to two pages?

questions.title: What does the class assignment prompt say?
questions.description: Is there a specific prompt, guiding question, or set of instructor guidelines you need to respond to?

questions.title: What tone and style are you aiming for?
questions.description: Do you want the writing to feel intimate and confessional, literary and lyrical, straightforward and factual, or something else?

questions.title: What does a successful submission look like to you?
questions.description: Are you aiming to meet a grading rubric, get instructor feedback, achieve a personal breakthrough, or simply produce a clean first draft?

questions.title: When is it due and what do you have so far?
questions.description: What is your deadline, and do you already have notes, an outline, or a rough draft to build from?
